summary: The Controller is the state's chief fiscal officer: she issues state payments, audits state and local spending, administers unclaimed property, and sits on the CalPERS and CalSTRS boards. Incumbent Democrat Malia Cohen, elected in 2022, placed first in the June 2 primary with 56.80%; Republican Herb Morgan, an investment executive, placed second with 37.53%.

positions.stance: Running on 'transparency, efficiency and fairness'; urged the Legislature and governor to spend cautiously during recent budget negotiations. (CalMatters voter guide)
Issued recommendations in September 2024 to prevent and detect charter-school fraud. (Wikipedia)
Campaigning on exposing fraud in state government, echoing fraud accusations the Trump administration has made against California. (CalMatters voter guide)

key_differences: Cohen is a career elected official who has served as a San Francisco supervisor, on the Board of Equalization, and as Controller. Morgan is a first-time candidate from investment management.
Morgan's campaign assumes widespread fraud in state spending. Cohen points to targeted audits and cautious budgeting.
An October 2026 federal lawsuit alleges that contractors for Cohen's office seized and sold foreign investors' unclaimed property without adequate notice. These are allegations, not findings.
